page: Microsoft Azure D64s_v6 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. It is configured with 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance across memory and compute-intensive tasks. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench multi-core and image processing tests, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read and write operations on large blocks scoring in the top 25%. Additionally, static web serving throughput is exceptional, reaching the top 10% tier. Cryptographic and compression tasks, including single-threaded gzip and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, also demonstrate strong performance. For AI workloads, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions support strong prompt processing speeds for small and medium language models, though text generation on larger 70B models falls into the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64s_v6 offers a balanced resource density suitable for enterprise workloads that require high-frequency CPU performance and robust memory bandwidth without the added cost of bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and intermediate-scale LLM inference. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which should be factored into the overall architectural design.
